ladder.why: The defining stack problem: the most recent unmatched opener must be the first one closed, which is exactly last-in first-out.

ladder.teaches: a stack augmented with extra data (min stack)
ladder.why: Storing the running minimum beside each entry shows how a stack can carry extra data that stays valid until that entry is popped.
An operand stack evaluates postfix in one pass: each operator pops its two operands (right first) and pushes the result.

ladder.teaches: simulate with undo or collapse (asteroids, removing pairs)
ladder.why: Survivors wait on a stack and each incoming left-mover collapses the top in a while loop, the template for every collision simulation.
Cascading removals of k equal neighbours become O(n) once each stack entry is a (character, run length) pair.
Matching with a stack of indices tells you which brackets are unmatched, not just whether the string is valid.
Nested k[...] groups are parsed by pushing the outer context (text so far, repeat count) at '[' and restoring it at ']'.

ladder.teaches: simulate with undo or collapse (asteroids, removing pairs)
ladder.why: Undo and redo are two stacks moving commands back and forth, with a new command clearing the redo stack.

ladder.teaches: simulate with undo or collapse (asteroids, removing pairs)
ladder.why: Asteroid Collision in an OA story with directions, strengths and indices: you must recognise the collapse-on-a-stack simulation.

ladder.teaches: simulate with undo or collapse (asteroids, removing pairs)
ladder.why: Deleting AB or BB means every B cancels the character before it; a stack (or just its size) handles deletions that expose new pairs.
Start/end logs are matched pairs on a call stack, and the top of the stack owns the time between events.

ladder.teaches: a stack augmented with extra data (min stack)
ladder.why: BEGIN/ROLLBACK/COMMIT is a stack of dictionaries, each layer holding the writes of one open transaction.

ladder.teaches: a stack augmented with extra data (min stack)
ladder.why: 'Add v to the bottom i elements' in O(1) needs a lazy increment stored on the stack and handed down on pop.
Parentheses with + and - need the stack to save the running result and sign at each '(' and combine them at ')'.
A stack of indices with the last unmatched ')' as its floor turns matching into the length of the longest valid run.

notes: Many problems in the stack pool are monotonic-stack problems (daily temperatures, remove k digits, shopkeeper final price, next smaller, predict answer, maximum profitable groups, erase pairs, sum of max subarrays, maximum sum of heights, largest square); they were moved to the monotonic-stack ladder. 'Evaluate an expression' is taught by RPN (Atlassian, outside the pools), Decode String and Basic Calculator (Amazon, outside the pools; its source statement was cut off and was restored from the canonical LC 224 in its fix).
